ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy e01faa1367fa (2026-05-12T14:13:20Z) modified TemplateCache.java and RenderEngine.java, removing the previously-configured Caffeine cache eviction policy (maximumSize + expireAfterWrite TTL). The updated code initializes the template cache as an unbounded ConcurrentHashMap with no TTL and no size cap. Under normal production traffic, the combination of many distinct template IDs, locales, and variant keys causes the cache to grow without bound. Within ~6 minutes of startup the JVM heap is exhausted by cache entries, triggering G1 Full GCs and ultimately OOM kills, leading to a CrashLoopBackOff cycle.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: kubectl rollout undo deployment/email-service -n prod to roll back to the previous image, stopping the CrashLoopBackOff. 2. Code fix in TemplateCache.java: reinstate the Caffeine cache configuration with maximumSize=1000 and expireAfterWrite=30m (or add application.properties keys template.cache.max-size and template.cache.ttl-minutes and wire them in). 3. Re-deploy the fixed build and verify heap_used stabilizes below 1GB and cache_entries is bounded in logs. 4. Add a JVM heap usage alert at 70% to catch future regressions earlier.
